courses.Course Overview: A renovated Gary Player design built around variety, strategy and classic Lowcountry scenery. Cougar Point mixes short and long par 4s, risk-reward par 5s and demanding par 3s with marsh, water and bunkering that reward disciplined shot selection. The course's defining stretch runs along the Kiawah River.
courses.History: Designed by Gary Player, Cougar Point underwent an extensive 10-month renovation with Gary Player Design and reopened in October 2017. The renovation modernized the course while preserving its strategic character and Lowcountry setting. A new Cougar Point clubhouse followed, overlooking the 18th hole and completing the updated golf experience.
courses.Playing Tips: Accuracy and course management matter more than raw distance. Pick conservative targets when water and marsh pinch the landing areas, and pay attention to approach angles—being on the correct side of the fairway can make a major difference. The risk-reward holes offer opportunities, but forcing the issue can quickly bring big numbers into play.
courses.Signature Holes: Holes 4–6 form Cougar Point's signature stretch along the Kiawah River, with sweeping marsh views and some of the course's most demanding shots. No. 4 begins the stretch with a long par 4, while the river and marsh become increasingly prominent through Nos. 5 and 6. No. 17 is another standout—a scenic short par 4 with water down the right and multiple strategic options from the tee.

courses.Course Overview: Pete and Alice Dye's legendary seaside championship course is the ultimate test of the week. Ten holes run directly along the Atlantic and the remaining eight run parallel to them, leaving virtually the entire course exposed to coastal wind. The Ocean Course demands committed swings, disciplined targets and patience from the opening tee through one of golf's great finishing stretches.
courses.History: Designed by Pete and Alice Dye and opened for the 1991 Ryder Cup, The Ocean Course immediately entered golf history with the dramatic "War by the Shore." It later hosted Rory McIlroy's record-setting victory in the 2012 PGA Championship and Phil Mickelson's historic 2021 PGA Championship win, when he became the oldest men's major champion. The Ocean Course will host the PGA Championship again in 2031.
courses.Playing Tips: Respect the wind—it can completely change club selection and strategy from one shot to the next. Favor safe angles over heroic carries, use your caddie, and expect conditions to change throughout the round. Missing on the correct side of greens is critical, particularly on the exposed back nine. Avoid chasing mistakes; bogey can be a good score and patience will win matches here.
courses.Signature Holes: The closing stretch provides the defining Championship Saturday experience. No. 14 is a spectacular exposed par 3 with an elevated green. No. 17 is the iconic all-carry par 3 over water, one of Pete Dye's signature tests. No. 18 is a demanding oceanfront finishing par 4 where the drive and approach are both exposed to the wind, with panoramic Atlantic and dune views framing the finish.

courses.Course Overview: A strategic Jack Nicklaus design that rewards accuracy, positioning and smart course management. Turtle Point moves through lagoons and maritime forest before reaching its memorable oceanfront stretch. Generous landing areas can be deceptive—approach angles, wind and precise iron play will determine who scores well.
courses.History: Designed by Jack Nicklaus, Turtle Point has long been one of Kiawah Island Golf Resort's championship courses. Nicklaus and his design team returned for an extensive renovation in 2016 that rebuilt green complexes and bunkers, added new tees, restored strategic features and converted the course to Platinum Paspalum while preserving the character of the original design.
courses.Playing Tips: Think position before distance. Favor the side of the fairway that gives the best angle into the green, and avoid forcing shots around the lagoons. The course becomes increasingly exposed as you reach the ocean holes, so account for wind and commit to your number. Patience is rewarded—Turtle Point offers birdie opportunities, but poor positioning can quickly turn into a lost hole.
courses.Signature Holes: Holes 14–16 make up Turtle Point's signature oceanfront stretch. No. 14 introduces the Atlantic beside a demanding par 3. No. 15 is widely considered the course's signature hole, a short strategic par 4 framed by dunes with multiple options from the tee. No. 16 is another exposed oceanfront par 3 where wind and pin position can dramatically change the shot.

ruleBook.Body: Players receive 90% of the difference between their full Course Handicap and the lowest full Course Handicap in the match, rounded to the nearest whole stroke.
ruleBook.Title: Best Ball Handicap Allocation

ruleBook.Body: Team Handicap is calculated using 35% of the lower-handicap player's Course Handicap plus 15% of the higher-handicap player's Course Handicap. Match strokes are determined from the difference between the two Team Handicaps.
ruleBook.Title: Scramble Handicap Allocation

ruleBook.Body: Players receive 100% of the difference between their full Course Handicap and their opponent's full Course Handicap, rounded to the nearest whole stroke.
ruleBook.Title: Singles Handicap Allocation

ruleBook.Body: Enter gross scores into The Bagger App. The Bagger automatically applies the tournament's handicap and net-scoring rules. Submit the completed scorecard after the match.
ruleBook.Title: Gross Score Entry

ruleBook.Body: Front 9 = 1 point. Back 9 = 1 point. Overall Match = 1 point. Maximum available: 3 points.
ruleBook.Title: Best Ball Scoring

ruleBook.Body: Front 9 = 1 point. Back 9 = 1 point. Overall Match = 1 point. Maximum available: 3 points.
ruleBook.Title: Scramble Scoring

ruleBook.Body: Each 18-hole Singles match is worth 3 points. A tied match awards 1.5 points to each team.
ruleBook.Title: Singles Scoring

ruleBook.Body: A tied hole is halved. There are no carryovers to the next hole.
ruleBook.Title: No Carryovers

ruleBook.Body: Double par is the maximum score on any hole to help maintain pace of play.
ruleBook.Title: Double-Par Maximum

ruleBook.Body: Lift, clean and place is permitted in the fairway. It is not permitted in the rough, bunkers, or native areas.
ruleBook.Title: Lift, Clean and Place

ruleBook.Body: A ball entering a penalty area receives a one-stroke penalty. Take relief under the applicable tournament/local rule and use a designated drop zone when provided.
ruleBook.Title: Penalty Areas

ruleBook.Body: If every player agrees that a ball should be in play but cannot be found because of leaves, a free drop is permitted. The player may tie the hole but may not win the hole. Opposing-team approval is required. This rule does not apply to fescue or other areas where the ball is reasonably lost.
ruleBook.Title: Leaf Rule

ruleBook.Body: Free relief is available when the ball is within two club lengths of a sprinkler head, the sprinkler head is within two club lengths of the green, and it interferes with the player's line to the hole. Relief must not be closer to the hole.
ruleBook.Title: Greenside Sprinkler Heads

ruleBook.Body: Caddies may read putts, provide course guidance, and assist with strategy.
ruleBook.Title: Caddie Guidance

ruleBook.Body: Practice shots are not permitted. Players may putt on the previous green after the hole is complete, provided pace of play is maintained.
ruleBook.Title: Practice After a Hole

ruleBook.Body: Distance-only GPS/rangefinder functionality is permitted. Wind-adjusted devices, apps, or functionality are not permitted.
ruleBook.Title: The Memo Rule

ruleBook.Body: Declare the mulligan before leaving the tee. Once declared, the mulligan becomes the ball in play and the original shot is void.
ruleBook.Title: Mulligan Election & Ball in Play

ruleBook.Body: No Shotgun Mulligans will be awarded in Best Ball.
ruleBook.Title: Best Ball Mulligans

ruleBook.Body: Each player receives two shotgun mulligans per nine holes.
ruleBook.Title: Scramble Mulligans

ruleBook.Body: No Shotgun Mulligans will be awarded in Singles
ruleBook.Title: Singles Mulligans

ruleBook.Body: After selecting the team's shot, both players may place the ball within one club length of the selected position, no closer to the hole. The ball must remain in the same condition: fairway to fairway, rough to rough, and bunker to bunker.
ruleBook.Title: Scramble Ball Placement
